news.title: Opinion: When should medical school start?
news.summary: STAT readers weigh in on shortening medical school, fixing pediatric emergency care, and more.

news.title: Opinion: How Kennedy and MAHA could help stop measles
news.summary: Kennedy and MAHA say they aren’t anti-vaccine. They can prove it by promoting the MMR vaccine, writes Brinda Adhikari.

news.title: CMS issues Medicare Advantage proposals aimed at boosting competition
news.summary: The Trump administration has proposed a slew of changes to Medicare Advantage and Part D designed to "revitalize care" in these markets.

news.title: UnitedHealth the latest insurer to sue over the 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings
news.summary: CVS Heath's Aetna is joining the ranks of insurers suing over its results in the 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings.

news.title: CMS to withdraw moratorium on new ACA broker registrations
news.summary: CMS had instituted the moratorium in late September as part of its broader push to combat fraud on the Affordable Care Act's exchanges.

news.title: Consumers believe AI will be key in making healthcare simpler: survey
news.summary: Americans want a healthcare experience that's simpler and easier to understand, and artificial intelligence may be the key to getting there, a new survey shows.

news.title: HLTH 2026: Elsevier upgrades ClinicalKey AI with full patient EHR context
news.summary: San Juan Regional Medical Center is using ClinicalKey AI to give clinicians faster access to evidence-based guidance combined with patient-specific EHR data, with the goal of improving care and easing workforce constraints.

news.title: Cigna Group Foundation making $31.5M in grants available to community organizations in 10 states
news.summary: Cigna is making $31.5 million in grant funding available over the next three years to nonprofits in 10 states that are aiming to tackle several key community health priorities.

news.title: Florida court tosses Tampa General Hospital's suit against Eli Lilly over 340B discounts
news.summary: The hospital initially sued the pharmaceutical company over a policy it implemented that requires providers to submit claims-level data on pharmacy and medical dispensing if they participate in 340B.

news.title: Healthcare purchasers must weigh hospital quality alongside their prices, Leapfrog says
news.summary: The hospital safety watchdog paired the latest release of its hospital safety scores with calls for policymakers, purchasers and other stakeholders to consider hospital price and quality transparency side by side.

news.title: Aetna unveils new program aimed at offering end-to-end support for moms and babies
news.summary: Aetna is rolling out a new program that aims to provide key end-to-end care for pregnant women, new mothers and infants.

news.title: UnitedHealthcare's new care model leans on community pharmacies
news.summary: UnitedHealthcare is teaming up with CPSEN for its UHC Pharmacy Care Hub model, a new program that aims to lean on community pharmacists to reach Medicaid patients.

news.title: Department of Labor moves to end expedited green cards for nurses, physical therapists
news.summary: The Trump administration proposed eliminating a longstanding exemption to the permanent labor certification program, the latest in a string of policies raising the bar for foreign-born healthcare workers seeking employer sponsorship.

news.title: HLTH 2026: Viz.ai’s chief clinical officer on takeaways, goals of AI collab with National Rural Health Association
news.summary: Viz.ai Chief Clinical Officer Andrew Ibrahim, M.D., sat down with Fierce to discuss the partnership’s first year.

news.title: Danaher teams up with Microsoft to boost ‘experimental execution’
news.summary: Danaher Corporation and Microsoft are teaming for a strategic partnership to develop smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem.

news.title: Merck’s TROP2 ADC extends survival in pivotal gastroesophageal cancer trial
news.summary: Merck & Co.’s sacituzumab tirumotecan has improved overall survival in a phase 3 cancer trial, delivering a second pivotal global victory for the TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate.

news.title: Researchers may have to ‘revise a lot’ of theories about dementia after uncovering plastics in brain
news.summary: The field of micro- and nanoplastics has drawn a lot of interest in recent years as concerns grow about the impact of contamination in the environment. These tiny plastic particles are created when plastic breaks down and are usually so small that they are invisible to the naked eye.

news.title: FDA pushes decision on Belite’s eye disease pill back to May
news.summary: The FDA is taking a little extra time to review Belite Bio’s application for its treatment for a rare genetic eye condition, pushing the expected action date back by three months into May next year.

news.title: ‘It’s a very healthy sector’: Biopharma gathers in London as M&A shines and China clouds loom
news.summary: As the grand hotels and cosy cafes filled with biopharma executives and investors for London Life Sciences Week, the weather was as temperamental as any other English November.

news.title: Chutes & Ladders—Teva loses R&D head as innovation pivot advances
news.summary: Teva’s R&D chief has resigned a week after the company's R&D day. The White House yanked its FDA commissioner nomination at the 11th hour. Quanterix restarted its search for a CEO. And more.

news.title: Bausch + Lomb and Celldex rocked by respective phase 2 flops
news.summary: Bausch + Lomb and Celldex have independently reported phase 2 flops. While Celldex ended work in the indication in response to the setback, Bausch + Lomb noted numerical improvements and exploratory analyses to make the case for talks about entering phase 3.

news.title: Anthropic board director Vas Narasimhan bets AI can help Novartis solve ‘biological latency’
news.summary: On the same day Anthropic staged a record-shattering IPO on Nasdaq, the artificial intelligence tech giant’s lone pharmaceutical board member, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, was in London pitching investors on how the Swiss drugmaker is using AI to shrink drug development timelines and one day solve “biological latency.”

news.title: Crown Biosciences stays put as $204M Adicon deal falls through
news.summary: Crown Biosciences looks destined to go unworn for a while longer after its planned $204 million acquisition by China's Adicon fell through.

news.title: Vaccine biotech Evaxion halts infectious disease, autoimmune work to focus on oncology
news.summary: Evaxion is refocusing its R&D efforts to solely focus on developing and advancing its cancer vaccines.

news.title: nChroma halves headcount, calls time on trial of potential HBV ‘cure’
news.summary: nChroma Bio’s workforce is facing a second round of layoffs in 12 months, with the Boston biotech halving its headcount and scrapping a trial of its lead hepatitis asset.

news.title: Isomorphic adds Merck to AI drug discovery roster days after $5B raise
news.summary: Isomorphic Labs’ big week just got bigger. Days after raising $5 billion, the AI-powered biotech has added Merck & Co. to a list of partners that now includes three of the top four drugmakers by revenue.

papers.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
papers.summary: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. Existing methods treat this as a visual restoration problem, yet severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone. Humans instead read it by reasoning over image context, logical patterns, and prior knowledge. This raises a fundamental question: Does TAISR need reasoning? papers.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching
papers.summary: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. Two records may match at the base level but not at the variant level: they share an underlying design while differing in attributes such as color or size. Final matching accuracy does not separately characterize the capabilities involved. To study this problem, we use e-commerce as a challenging real-world domain. papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. papers.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
papers.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. papers.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
papers.summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition.
